score.scope: Still-image technical craft across the entire frame: visible construction, contact, material distinction, contours and coherent spatial integration. No score for an unbuilt 3D rig or animation.
score.confidence: high for the inspected visible surfaces and contacts; moderate for tiny or occluded anatomy
score.changeReason: The increase follows visible repairs in the actual export. The whole-frame material segmentation of 11 has been replaced by calmer, material-specific forms, including the bench, glasses, laptop, canopy, tree and path. The raised mallet now has a solid rounded grip and short readable wrist connection. Composition, identity, supports and corrected companion eyes survive. Plan acceptance and the desired score did not provide evidence for this increase.

It is much finer and less intrusive than 11, and no longer spreads as the same broken contour treatment across hard props, but it still feels somewhat embossed rather than entirely plush or velvet.

criteriaForNine: Met: soft character volume, cloth weave, coherent wood grain, continuous glasses/metal contours and readable stone/foliage distinguish materials across the complete image, not only around the hero.
Met: the native and 5x final grip clearly show a rounded hand enclosing the mallet handle and connecting through a short wrist/arm, without elongated fingers or a hollow strap shape.
Met: native, 1280 and 880 views retain the scene's support/contact and cinematic depth; the 420 view keeps the coding silhouette dominant without enlarging guests.
Met: the actual integrated companion crop preserves dark Muse eyes, one clean smile, and two pupil-free white Grok ovals. No visible local cleanup seam was found.
Met within visible anatomy: compact proportions, complete antenna paddles and plausible visible wings/feet remain. Hidden topology is outside this score.

W1.assessment: The repair reaches the whole picture. Bench boards and arm contours are continuous; the laptop lid and glasses rims have clean edges; the blanket retains intentional yarn/weave; table, toolbox and canopy forms are calmer; bark, stone and foliage retain their own shapes instead of the common angular overlay seen in 11. Cream and green forms shade smoothly again. Fine residual relief is acknowledged above but no longer breaks material separation or frame coherence. 07 remains a useful control; the result is not merely a blanket rollback.

W2.assessment: The angular cream/black sliver in 11 is replaced by one solid rounded grip around the handle. The short cream connection to the moth is readable; the tool appears held at native and whole-frame scale. The existing raised pose remains anticipation, so mallet-to-box impact is neither required nor claimed.

preservation: The coding moth remains alone on the foreground bench with the silver Apple MacBook and established cup/books/blanket. Guests stay in the two rear groups; there is no new cast, text or prop expansion.

All three moth appearances remain compact, large-headed and innocent, with unequal paddle antennae, small attached feet, visible marked layered wings and no stretched adult limbs. Far-side structures remain naturally occluded.

The hero sits into the bench and the laptop rests across the lap; the visible hand meets the keyboard plane. Cup-to-book and book-to-bench contacts remain plausible. Clawd and Dot occupy separate supported stools; the workshop table and tied canopy retain convincing support.

Muse and Grok remain grounded around one leaf. Native and 5x final-export crops show the Muse smile cleanup without a visible extra dark curve or patch boundary, and Grok's white oval interiors show no visible pupil spot. Clawd retains both square dark eyes; the blue Dot retains its beret.

The path still joins the resting tree, workshop and foreground bench into a continuous park. Scale, overlap, foreground framing and the softer distant bridge establish coherent depth. Warm upper-right light remains motivated across characters and environment.

The 1280 and 880 images read more calmly than 11 without losing the lush setting. At 420 the coding figure and laptop remain primary; fine guest actions naturally become secondary detail, not a reason to alter the established cast or composition.
optional: Retain the fine-relief and mitten-shape observations as future material/derivative guidance, not a request for another corrective pass.
